segments.text: Every night, Gumgumi looks up at the same moon.
The Moon is constantly circling around Earth.
But its markings never seem to change.
Turns out, the Moon is spinning too.
Earth pulls harder on the Moon's near side, stretching it slightly.
Long ago the Moon spun faster, so that stretch kept drifting out of line.
Earth's pull kept tugging it back, slowly braking the spin.
Eventually its spin matched its orbit exactly.
So the Moon always shows us the very same face.
